title: Remittances reach $2.5 billion in 24 days of November, up 6.4%
excerpt: Migrants sent $2.499 billion in the first 24 days of November, Bangladesh Bank data show, and $13.97 billion since July, 11.8% more than a year earlier.
content:
Bangladeshis working abroad sent $2.499 billion home in the first 24 days of November, 6.4% more than in the same period last year, according to Bangladesh Bank's daily data, bdnews24.com reported on Wednesday (25 November).

In the same 24 days of November 2025, remittances were $2.349 billion. At this year's daily average of about $104 million, the month would end at about $3.12 billion, which would be the first month above $3 billion since May, when $3.44 billion came in. Bangladesh Bank spokesperson and executive director Arif Hossain Khan told bdnews24.com the bank expected about $3.25 billion by the end of the month.

From 1 July to 24 November, the first months of the 2026-27 financial year, remittances totalled $13.97 billion, 11.8% more than the $12.50 billion of a year earlier. October brought $2.874 billion, up 12.1% year on year. In the 2025-26 financial year, migrants sent a record $35.59 billion, 17.34% more than the year before.

Why it matters

Remittances are now the strongest of the main economic indicators and a lifeline for millions of households, especially in districts with high migration. But the money comes at a cost to workers: an OKUP study of cheated migrants found most had no written contract, and only 28 of 85 complaints it followed were resolved. Growth in remittances is not the same as safer migration.

What to watch

  • The full November figure, due in early December.
  • Whether the reopening of the Malaysian market (see today's story) adds workers at lower cost.
